title: Africell Sierra Leone's $2 million upfront payment under the Sierratel MVNO partnership
description: The ministry's account of the relaunch of Sierratel, established 1995, as an MVNO in partnership with Africell Sierra Leone. The Government provides the national brand and policy direction; Africell brings network infrastructure and technical expertise, letting Sierratel generate revenue without upfront public investment. The President formally handed over a US$2 million upfront payment from Africell, designated to begin settling long-standing staff liabilities.

title: Orange Sierra Leone's EUR 23 million Bo data centre — national disaster-recovery hub
description: The ministry's account of the President's commissioning of Orange Sierra Leone's new EUR 23 million data centre in Bo City — the country's second such facility, working alongside the main Freetown centre to keep essential systems operational during outages or disruptions, and extending digital and financial services to Makeni, Kono and Kenema. No rack, floor-area or power figures are given for either facility.

title: Orange Sierra Leone's $50 million network modernisation to 4G/5G readiness
description: The ministry's account of Orange Sierra Leone's continuing network build-out: over 616 sites nationwide, 70% green-energy powered, 40 new sites built in the stated year, and a US$50 million investment programme to modernise the network to full 4G/5G readiness. The commissioning of a new site at Mathonkara, Tenie Chiefdom, Tonkolili District is the dated event the figure is attached to.

title: Technical assistance to Statistics Sierra Leone for the 2026 population census
description: The grant will support the technical capacity and operational readiness of Statistics Sierra leone (Stata-SL) to conduct cartographic mapping and the pilot census. Specifically the grant will strengthen Stats-SL capacity to (i) undertake digital census mapping and (ii) use a digital census system. The grant will support a cartography /GIS exper and an IT expert who build the capacity of and support Stats-SL staff.

title: Sierra Leone Compact — Millennium Challenge Corporation's $480 million power-sector programme
description: MCC's own programme page for the largest standing United States commitment to Sierra Leone: a $480 million compact signed 27 September 2024, comprising three projects — Distribution and Access ($123,634,000 project total), Power Sector Reform ($50,490,000) and Transmission Backbone ($226,702,000) — addressing insufficient, unreliable electricity supply. The compact builds on Sierra Leone's MCC threshold programme that concluded in 2021.

title: Sierra Leone Compact \u2014 Distribution Dispatch Center (Distribution and Access Project, Activity 2.1)
description: Activity 2.1 of MCC's $480.7M Sierra Leone Compact (signed September 2024) constructs and operationalises a main and backup distribution dispatch center for EDSA, providing centralised visibility and remote operating capability over the distribution network. The dispatch center improves EDSA's operations and maintenance performance, enables real-time monitoring of the distribution system, and supports efficient management of an increasingly complex network including integration of variable renewable generation. The $30.6M activity is part of the $123.6M Distribution and Access Project. This is distinct from the Transmission Dispatch Center (Activity 1.1) which serves EGTC; this center serves the distribution utility EDSA.
recipient_organisation: Electricity Distribution and Supply Authority (EDSA), Government of Sierra Leone / MCA-Sierra Leone

title: Sierra Leone Compact \u2014 Transmission Dispatch Center and SCADA Upgrades (Transmission Backbone Project, Activity 1.1)
description: Activity 1.1 of MCC's $480.7M Sierra Leone Compact (signed September 2024) establishes a national transmission dispatch center with supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) system for EGTC. The dispatch center provides centralised visibility and remote operating capability over the transmission network, enabling real-time monitoring and control of the 225kV transmission backbone. SCADA upgrades improve grid reliability, accelerate response to network disruptions, facilitate integration of variable renewable generation sources, and support future regional integration with neighbouring countries. The dispatch center also includes a backup facility. The $23.4M activity is part of the $226.7M Transmission Backbone Project. No digital identity or payments components; purely energy sector operational technology / SCADA digitisation.
recipient_organisation: Electricity Generation and Transmission Company (EGTC), Government of Sierra Leone / MCA-Sierra Leone

title: SAP033: Green Climate Fund financing for Sierra Leone's Multi-Hazard Impact-based Forecasting and Early Warning System
description: The GCF's own project page for SAP033: total project value US$21.1m (US$15,094,264 GCF grant plus US$6,006,620 co-financing), approved by the GCF Board 25 October 2023, Funded Activity Agreement executed 12 December 2025 and effective 10 June 2026, completion due 10 June 2031. Builds a Multi-Hazard Impact-based Forecasting and Early Warning and Early Action System and trains local climate agencies. Project documents on the page are labelled "AfDB SAP033", identifying the African Development Bank as the Accredited Entity implementing the grant on GCF's behalf.

title: Sierra Leone Digital Transformation Project
description: Supports Sierra Leone's digital transformation through broadband infrastructure, digital government systems, digital financial services, and digital skills development.

title: Innovative Model Combining Block Farming and a Digital Platform to Enable a Sustainable Pineapple Supply Chain
description: This model combines block-farming with a Digital Extension Tools. On a 50ha block-farm, 250 farmers will be hired to work on their own 0,5 acre plot, creating stable jobs for 20-30% women and 40-50% youth.

title: Digital Connectivity in Schools to Accelerate COVID-19 Education Response \u2014 Sierra Leone (Giga Phase 2)
description: Joint project between UNICEF Sierra Leone and the Islamic Development Bank (IsDB) to connect 523 schools to the internet. The IsDB approved a USD 5 million loan in September 2021 (Sierra Leone Parliament ratified October 2022). Under the co-financing arrangement, IsDB covers connectivity for 403 schools and UNICEF covers 120 schools. Building on the Giga Phase 1 pilot that connected 42 schools. Project aims to scale to 11,000 schools ultimately. Sierra Leone connected 39 hard-to-reach schools by 2023 (Giga Annual Results 2023). Internet costs reduced from USD 12,000 to USD 1,500 per school per year (87.5% reduction). Part of Giga's global initiative (UNICEF-ITU).

title: Escotel Sierra Leone \u2013 Solar Power for Telecom Towers Guarantee
description: MIGA political risk guarantee of $13.5 million to Escotel Mauritius covering its investment in Escotel (SL) Limited, which installs and operates solar-hybrid power systems at telecom tower sites (TNS) in Sierra Leone. Escotel installs solar PV panels replacing diesel generators at ~600 telecom network sites owned/operated by Orange Sierra Leone. Reduces diesel fuel use by 75% and avoids 58,000 tCO2e over the guarantee period. Risks: Transfer Restriction, Expropriation, War and Civil Disturbance for up to 10 years.

title: China Eximbank provides RMB 207 million government concessional loan for Phase 2 of National Fibre Optic Backbone Infrastructure Project (Linked to Project ID#30254)
description: On June 23, 2019, the Chinese Government and the Government of Sierra Leone signed a preferential loan framework agreement for Phase 2 of the National Fibre Optic Backbone Infrastructure Project. Then, on August 26, 2019, China Eximbank and the the Government of Sierra Leone’s Ministry of Finance signed an RMB 207,000,000 government concessional loan (GCL) agreement [CHINA EXIMBANK GCL NO (2019) 10 TOTAL No. (681)] for Phase 2 of the National Fibre Optic Backbone Infrastructure Project. The GCL agreement was then ratified by Sierra Leone’s Parliament on September 19, 2019. The borrowing terms of the GCL are as follows: a 20-year maturity, a 5-year grace period, a 1% interest rate, a 0.25% (RMB 517,500) management fee, and a 0.25% commitment fee. The borrower is responsible for repaying the loan between 2024 and 2039. Under the terms of the agreement, Government of Sierra Leone’s Ministry of Finance is also responsible for on-lending the proceeds of the GCL to a state-owned enterprise in Sierra Leone known as Sierra Leone Cable Company Limited (SALCAB). SALCAB, in turn, is expected to use the proceeds of the GCL to finance a $30 million commercial contract (ID#0002881900010V) between the Government of Sierra Leone’s Ministry of Information and Communications and Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd., which was signed on April 11, 2019. SALCAB signed an on-lending agreement with the Ministry of Finance on August 22, 2019.   The purpose of the project is to lay a 721.5-kilometer fiber-optic network that covers 15 major cities in the northern, eastern and southern regions of Sierra Leone.  Upon completion, the telecommunications infrastructure is expected to allow telecommunications operators to offer 3G and 4G services.   Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd. is the EPC contractor responsible for implementation. title: SONATEL Mobile Telecom Services \u2013 Orange Sierra Leone Guarantee
description: MIGA issued guarantees of $97.2 million to Senegalese telecommunications company SONATEL S.A. covering its 50% equity stake in mobile operator Orange Sierra Leone Ltd (OSL). The acquisition facilitates modernization and expansion of OSL's network in Sierra Leone through deployment of additional telecom towers, improvement in network services, quality and reliability. Supported by IDA18 Private Sector Window (PSW) MIGA Guarantee Facility. Risks covered: expropriation and war & civil disturbance for up to 15 years.

title: Rural Renewable Energy Project (RREP) — FCDO financing of Sierra Leone's rural electrification programme
description: The Rural Renewable Energy Project (RREP), client the Government of Sierra Leone's Ministry of Energy, donor the UK's FCDO with a contribution of GBP 37,739,328, implemented by UNOPS. Runs October 2016 to May 2022. Builds 94 solar-powered mini-grids and 3 stand-alone systems at community health centres, aiming to provide up to 4 MW of renewable electricity to rural communities. Three private operators each signed a Public Private Partnership Agreement with the Ministry in December 2018, leveraging US$10m of private investment.
recipient_organisation: Ministry of Energy, Government of Sierra Leone
